article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Evening Brief
article.dek: Lamar is officially questionable and the Ravens line flipped sides, Kmet's season is over, and the Value card found a new home in Paris.

items.headline: Lamar officially questionable — and the line flipped sides
paragraphs: The Ravens listed Lamar Jackson as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals. Jackson confirmed it's a high ankle sprain, said he's 'heading in the right direction,' and the call is game-time — Tyler Huntley would start if he can't go.

The market heard it. This morning the board had the Ravens -1.5 at both books. Tonight it has the Bengals -1.5 — the line flipped sides on one designation. The moneyline moved from Ravens -118 to near pick'em, and the total's price shifted to the Under at -115.
The app's model still has this game about a pick'em (expected margin roughly -0.31), and the evening board's QB row now lists Lamar as questionable instead of Huntley.
items.takeaway: A flipped line on a game-time QB call: don't bet this game Friday — wait for the decision, then Check your number.

items.headline: Kmet's season is over
paragraphs: Bears coach Ben Johnson confirmed it Friday afternoon: tight end Cole Kmet is headed to injured reserve with the serious right-knee injury from Thursday night's 30-24 win over the Patriots. His season is done.

More of the tight-end work now shifts to rookie Colston Loveland, who caught a touchdown Thursday. The Bears don't play again until next week, so there's nothing to bet here tonight — just a roster fact for next week's board.
items.takeaway: Bears 5-2, Patriots 4-3 — and Chicago's tight-end room is Loveland's now.

items.headline: Mayfield expected back — but three Bucs ruled out
paragraphs: Baker Mayfield practiced fully all week and coach Todd Bowles said Friday he's expected to start Sunday at Carolina, back from the dislocated right thumb that cost him three games. He's officially listed questionable.

The market moved on it: Tampa +3 went from -105 to -115 at DraftKings, and FanDuel is down to Panthers -2.5. The board's QB row flipped from Jalon Daniels to Mayfield — and the Value card rotated off Tampa to New Orleans.

One catch: the Bucs ruled out receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), right tackle Luke Goedeke (calf), and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib). A returning starter behind a backup right tackle, without his top receiver.
items.takeaway: The QB upgrade is real, the supporting cast is thinner — and the number already moved. Check your price, don't chase the news.

items.headline: Final injury report roundup
paragraphs: San Francisco heads to Atlanta shorthanded: the 49ers ruled out wide receivers Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) plus pass rusher Nick Bosa (calf). Christian Kirk, Upton Stout, and Siran Neal are questionable.

The good-news side of Friday: Patrick Mahomes practiced fully and isn't on the Chiefs' injury report (knee). The Dolphins ruled out cornerback Reese Taylor and listed two more as doubtful/questionable against the Jets. Saints left tackle Asim Richards (thumb) practiced fully with no designation and is expected to play in Paris.
Also cleared with no designation Friday: Jaylen Waddle (Broncos), Tony Pollard (Titans), Jonathan Taylor and Keenan Allen (Colts), Rashid Shaheed (Seahawks), and Bucky Irving (Bucs).
items.takeaway: The 49ers are the weekend's biggest absence list; most other Friday designations leaned positive.

items.headline: Weather: nothing today
paragraphs: No NFL games on Friday, so there's no kickoff weather to check. Sunday's outdoor kickoff-window forecasts firm up closer to Sunday and will be covered in the Sunday morning edition.
items.takeaway: Friday is a weather off-day; check back Sunday morning before you lock anything in.

items.headline: Your three cards tonight
paragraphs: Hit Rate: Vikings moneyline -295 (FanDuel), Colts at Vikings. The model's win probability is 78.6% — the most likely to win on the board. Notice the evaluator EV is -0.033: Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate, and that's not a flaw — it's the job description.

Balanced: Browns moneyline -126 (FanDuel), Browns at Titans. Unchanged from this morning — model 71.9%, EV +0.027. The middle ground: a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor.

Value: Saints +3 -108 (DraftKings), Steelers at Saints in Paris. Always the model's +EV play (EV +0.034). It rotated off Tampa +3 this evening once Mayfield money made that number worse — the card follows the price, not the team.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate = most likely to win. Balanced = strong without overpaying. Value = the +EV play. Check = the verdict on your price.

items.headline: Monday night: the model and the market still disagree
paragraphs: Cowboys at Eagles: the model's expected margin has this about a pick'em, while the market board has Dallas -4.5 at both books. Nothing changed today — the model didn't budge, and the price barely did.
Tanner McKee makes his second straight start for Philadelphia with Jalen Hurts on injured reserve. When the model says pick'em and the market says -4.5, don't guess — run your number through Check.

items.headline: The board caught up — but Sunday decides
paragraphs: The evening board's quarterback rows now reflect the day's news: Mayfield in for Tampa, McCarthy in for the Giants, Lamar listed questionable for Baltimore. The morning's stale rows are fixed.
But Lamar is a true game-time decision, and inactives become official about 90 minutes before kickoff. If your book still shows this afternoon's number, run it through Check now — and again Sunday.
items.takeaway: Fresh QB rows tonight, one game-time decision left — Check now, Check again when inactives drop.

items.headline: Learn the Game: steam move
paragraphs: (Hypothetical example:) Imagine a team opens as a 2.5-point favorite on Monday. Friday afternoon, news breaks that their starting quarterback might not play. By Saturday morning, the other team is a 1.5-point favorite. That fast swing on fresh information is called a steam move.

What could it mean? The market decided the news mattered more than the opener did — it's information moving the line, not a slow pile of public bets. What to watch next: whether the line settles or keeps running, and where your model lands once it sees the same news.

How to apply it: don't chase the move after it ran. If you like the new side, type the current number into Check and let the app price what's left — the value may already be gone, and Check will tell you.
items.takeaway: A steam move tells you the market heard news — Check tells you whether there's still a price worth playing.

items.headline: Friday: the flip, the QB money, and the steam
paragraphs: The headliner: Ravens-Bengals flipped sides. Ravens -1.5 this morning became Bengals -1.5 tonight at both books after Lamar's questionable designation, with the moneyline sliding to near pick'em. The app's QB row caught it (Lamar, questionable).

Quarterback money elsewhere: Tampa +3 went from -105 to -115 at DraftKings on Mayfield's return, and FanDuel is down to Panthers -2.5 — the Value card rotated from Tampa to New Orleans +3 (-108 at DraftKings). Vikings moneyline steamed from -278 to -298, and the Hit Rate card moved with it to FanDuel -295.

The rest: Browns -1.5 to -2.5 at DraftKings (moneyline -130 to -135, total down to 36.5); Broncos -230 to -238; Chiefs +3 -120 to -115 and moneyline +120 to +124 on Mahomes's clean bill; Raiders +3.5 to +3.0 at DraftKings — down from an opener of +7, the week's big mover. Saints +3 ticked from -102 to -108.

One timing note, and only one: Ravens-Bengals is a wait — Lamar is a game-time decision and inactives land about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. For everything else, if your book has this afternoon's number and Check says bet, bet now — waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.

And the standing reminder: when the board hasn't picked up a move, or your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel, tap Check, type in your book's line and price — the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: A news-heavy Friday moved four games and rotated a card — Check your number before Sunday's public money arrives.

items.headline: Friday night: Check your Sunday prices
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, and today it moved: a flipped side in Baltimore, quarterback money in Tampa, a pricier favorite in Minnesota. Before you lock anything in for Sunday, run each price through Check — type in your book's line and price and get a bet/no-bet verdict on the number you can actually play.
Sunday brings the late rush of public money on big-name teams, and that rush usually moves numbers the wrong way for price-sensitive bettors. Tonight's number can be better than Sunday's.
items.takeaway: Check Friday's numbers tonight — a good price today beats a hoped-for price Sunday.
